description: Turn the recurring detector's existing intelligence into proactive alerts. The detector already computes price changes, expected next dates, and staleness — but that knowledge sits passively on the recurring page waiting to be noticed. This feature bridges detections into the existing notification pipeline: subscription price creep, missed expected income, and newly detected recurring commitments become deliverable events with per-member subscriptions, cooldowns, and dedup. Deterministic end to end — no LLM.

timing.plannedEarliestExecution: after Feature 24 merges (migration numbering coordination only — no functional dependency)
timing.gatingCondition: None functionally. Recurring substrate (Features 19/22) and notification foundation (migrations 019/020, brrr transport, send-notifications.js runner) already exist. Independent of Feature 23 push reminders. Take the next available migration number after Feature 24's 023.

principles: Alert on what the detector already knows — this feature adds event plumbing, not new inference, except for missed-income timing
Missed income must fire on the stream's own schedule tolerance (expected_next_date + tolerance_days), not the 2x-interval stale heuristic — a late paycheck matters in days, not weeks
Every alert is deterministic and explains itself with numbers: prior amount, new amount, percent, expected date, days late
One notification per distinct event: source_key dedup + cooldown via existing notification_event_state, so a price change alerts once, not on every sync
Ignored and likely_cancelled streams never alert; paused streams never alert
Alerts respect per-member subscriptions exactly like existing event types — parents subscribe, kids are out of scope
In-app visibility mirrors every notification: the recurring page shows the same alerts, so nothing is notification-only
No LLM anywhere in this feature — these are the highest signal-per-word notifications a cash-flow app can send precisely because they are just numbers
SECRETS INVARIANT: notification payloads contain merchant display names, amounts, and dates only — no account numbers, tokens, or institution identifiers

techStack.database: PostgreSQL — one migration extending the event_type CHECK constraints (pattern from migration 020) and adding a recurring_alert_events table for event provenance
techStack.integrationPoints: lib/recurring-detector.js post-detection hook, lib/notification-rules.js EVENT_TYPES registry + evaluateNotificationCandidates, scripts/send-notifications.js runner (unchanged), public/recurring.html alert surfacing, admin notification settings
techStack.testing: node:test for event generation, thresholds, dedup, and subscription gating with fixture streams; Playwright for recurring page alert rendering and admin toggles

deferredForV1: Missed expense/bill alerts (autopay failed) — same mechanism as missed income; ship income first where the household stakes are clearest, then extend by config
Price-drop notifications (direction = down) — visible on the recurring page already; not worth a push in v1
Digest-style batching of multiple alerts into one notification

userStories.title: Price creep on a recurring stream raises an event
acceptanceCriteria: When the detector records a price change with direction = 'up' and price_change_pct >= the configured threshold (app_config price_creep_threshold_pct, default 5), a recurring_price_creep event candidate is created
The event payload includes merchant name, prior amount, new amount, percent change, and frequency — enough to act on without opening the app
source_key is derived from the stream identity plus price_change_date so one price change alerts exactly once, regardless of how many syncs re-observe it
Streams with status ignored, paused, or likely_cancelled never generate price events
A subsequent distinct price change on the same stream (new price_change_date) is a new event
Downward price changes generate no notification in v1
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with fixture streams: at-threshold fires, below-threshold does not, dedup across repeated evaluation, status exclusions, and repeat-change re-fire.

userStories.title: Missed expected income alerts within days, not weeks
acceptanceCriteria: An active income stream whose expected_next_date + tolerance_days has passed with no new occurrence in recurring_expense_history generates a recurring_missed_income event
The check runs as part of the existing post-sync recurring refresh so a deposit that arrived in the same sync cancels the candidate before evaluation
The event payload includes merchant name, expected date, days overdue, and typical amount
source_key is derived from the stream identity plus the specific missed expected_next_date so one missed occurrence alerts once, and the next missed occurrence is a distinct event
When the income eventually arrives, no retraction notification is sent in v1 — the recurring page simply returns to healthy state
Override fields (override_expected_next_date) are respected as the authoritative expected date when set
The existing stale/likely_cancelled status transitions are unchanged — this alert is additive and faster, not a replacement
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with date-controlled fixtures: fires at expected+tolerance+1, does not fire within tolerance, same-sync arrival suppresses, override date respected, per-occurrence dedup.

userStories.title: New recurring commitment detection catches silent subscriptions
acceptanceCriteria: When the detector inserts a recurring_expenses row that did not previously exist (new stream identity) with cashflow_type = 'expense' and confidence medium or high, a recurring_new_commitment event is generated — the free-trial-quietly-converted case
The event payload includes merchant name, amount, frequency, and first/last seen dates
New income streams do not notify in v1 (new paychecks are never a surprise to the household)
Streams first detected during a historical backfill or initial detection run do not flood notifications — a one-time high-water mark (streams existing before this feature's migration) is exempt
source_key is the stream identity so a given commitment alerts exactly once ever
Low-confidence new streams do not notify but remain visible on the recurring page as today
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: new medium/high expense stream fires, income does not, low confidence does not, pre-existing streams exempt via migration marker, once-ever dedup.

userStories.title: Events ride the existing notification pipeline end to end
acceptanceCriteria: Migration extends the event_type CHECK constraints on member_notification_subscriptions, notification_event_state, and notification_delivery_log with the three new types (exact pattern from migration 020)
The three event types are registered in lib/notification-rules.js EVENT_TYPES with household-friendly labels and descriptions, and evaluateNotificationCandidates emits their candidates

Per-member subscriptions, interruption levels, cooldowns, and delivery logging work identically to existing event types with zero changes to scripts/send-notifications.js beyond what candidate evaluation provides
price_creep_threshold_pct is configurable in the admin notification settings alongside existing thresholds
Each new event type can be independently enabled/disabled per member like existing types
Notification copy follows the existing 'Family Pulse:' prefix convention and stays under a phone lock-screen-friendly length
userStories.testStrategy: node:test extending notification-rules.test.js: registry shape, candidate emission, subscription gating, cooldown state writes; dry-run pass through send-notifications flow with fixtures.

userStories.title: Recurring page mirrors every alert in-app
acceptanceCriteria: The recurring page shows an alerts strip summarizing active health events: price creep (existing Up X% badge extended), missed income (days overdue), and recent new commitments
Each alert links or scrolls to the affected stream card
Alert history is inspectable: a recurring_alert_events table records generated events with timestamps so 'did Pulse tell me about this?' is answerable
The strip renders correctly on mobile (iOS web wrapper) — single-column stacking, no horizontal scroll
Kids do not see the alerts strip (recurring page access rules unchanged)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for alert-history endpoint shape and role gating; Playwright for strip rendering, mobile viewport, and stream-card linkage.

medium: Missed-income false positives from schedule drift (weekday-anchored deposits like SSA shift dates month to month). Mitigation: per-stream tolerance_days is already tuned per frequency window, overrides are authoritative, and Feature 22's anchor-drop fix removed the duplicate-stream source of drift; monitor and widen tolerance per stream if needed.

Notification fatigue if thresholds are too sensitive. Mitigation: 5% default price-creep threshold, once-ever/once-per-occurrence dedup, per-member opt-in per event type, and existing cooldown machinery.
low: Initial-detection flood of new-commitment alerts. Mitigation: migration high-water mark exempts all pre-existing streams.

Amount-band noise on variable recurring charges (e.g. utilities) misread as price creep. Mitigation: detector already bands amounts with tolerance; threshold applies to the banded change the detector itself reports.
Migration numbering collision with in-flight Feature 24. Mitigation: take the next available number at implementation time; PRD deliberately does not hardcode one.
operational: brrr transport availability is a household infrastructure dependency shared with existing notifications — no new failure mode, but alerts inherit its outages.
If Feature 23 (push reminders foundation) later changes transports, these events must migrate with the existing four event types as a unit.

preFlightChecklist: Confirm default price_creep_threshold_pct (recommended 5) and whether it should be absolute-dollar-gated too (e.g. ignore creep under $2/month even if over threshold)
Decide missed-income evaluation timing: post-sync hook only (recommended — three syncs daily is fresh enough) vs. its own cron
Confirm the new-commitment confidence floor (recommended: medium)
Verify per-stream tolerance_days values look sane on the live recurring_expenses table before trusting them as the missed-income grace period
Decide whether recurring_alert_events history needs a retention cap (recommended: keep forever — it is tiny)
Take the next available migration number after Feature 24 lands
